data.description: Luca | 20 places Updated: March 19, 2026 Overview Are you preparing for your trip to Japan? Here is all the information you need before boarding your fl ight. In addition to some cultural tips, which never hurt, I will help you with practical matters, such as booking your travel, what to do with your luggage, and reserving the best restaurants throughout Japan. Look in the guide for apps to download (marked with the symbol ) and then you will have nothing to worry about. Places and Experiences 17 Attractions 3 Locations What you need to know before you go Things not to do Public Behavior • Speaking loudly on trains or buses → is considered very rude, even on the phone. • Eating while walking → is not illegal, but is seen as lacking elegance. It’s better to sit in a designated area. • Blowing your nose in public → is considered disgusting; it’s preferred to step away and do it privately. • Not respecting the queue → Japanese people are very orderly; skipping the line or not following it creates discomfort. • Organized queues → are always respected, at ticket o ffi ces as well as for public transport. • Escalators → in Tokyo, you stand on the left, in Osaka on the right. • Trash and Civic Rules → in Japan public bins are few. data.name: Itsukushima Jinja
data.description: Itsukushima Shrine, reached by ferry from Hiroshima, boasts a striking vermillion torii gate. The island features free- roaming deer, scenic views from Mount Misen, and charming shops.

data.name: Saidouji Temple
data.description: Saidouji Temple in Niimi, Okayama, is an 8th-century Buddhist site known for its tranquil ambiance, stunning architecture, and lush surroundings, o ff ering a serene retreat for re fl ection.

data.name: Kintaikyo Bridge
data.description: Kintaikyo Bridge, a stunning wooden arch bridge in Iwakuni, Yamaguchi Prefecture, Japan, was originally constructed in 1673. Its fi ve elegant arches and scenic views, especially during cherry blossom season, make it a cherished symbol of the city and a must-visit attraction.

data.name: Kifune Shrine
data.description: Kifune Shrine, a sacred Shinto site in Kyoto's hills, honors the water deity. Surrounded by verdant nature, it o ff ers tranquility away from urban life. A charming lantern-lit path leads to this 8th-century shrine, renowned for blessings of safe travels and stunning vistas, attracting both locals and visitors.

data.name: Tsubosaka-dera
data.description: Tsubosaka-dera, a historic Buddhist temple in Nara Prefecture, Japan, dates back to the 7th century. Renowned for its Kannon statue, serene paths, and seasonal cherry blossoms, it o ff ers a tranquil escape rich in cultural heritage.

data.name: Enoshima
data.description: Enoshima, a picturesque island in Kanagawa Prefecture, Japan, boasts scenic vistas, cultural landmarks, and outdoor adventures, making it a favored day trip from Tokyo.

data.name: Mount Kachikachi Super View Swing
data.description: Japan +81 555-75-2929 Mount Kachikachi Super View Swing provides stunning views of Mount Fuji and Lake Kawaguchi. Accessible via a scenic ropeway, it o ff ers thrilling swings and beautiful walking paths for nature enthusiasts.

data.name: Hakone Shrine
data.description: Hakone Shrine, situated at the base of Mount Hakone, is famous for its iconic torii gate in Lake Ashi. Founded in 757 AD, it honors mountain deities. Surrounded by serene cedar forests, visitors can explore scenic paths, engage in traditional rituals, and appreciate the site's deep historical signi fi cance.
data.address: 80-1 Motohakone, Hakone, Ashigarashimo District, Kanagawa 250-0522, Japan

data.name: Mishima Sky Walk
data.description: Mishima Sky Walk, Japan's longest pedestrian suspension bridge at 400 meters, o ff ers breathtaking views of Mount Fuji and Suruga Bay, complemented by observation points and trails, perfect for nature enthusiasts and families. Kamikochi Visitor Center, Chubu Sangaku

data.name: National Park
data.description: Nestled in the stunning Chubu Sangaku National Park, the Kamikochi Visitor Center is a must-visit for hikers and nature enthusiasts. It o ff ers vital information, educational exhibits, and trail maps to enhance your exploration of the breathtaking Kamikochi Valley.

data.name: Nachi Waterfall
data.description: Nachi Waterfall, a majestic 133-meter cascade in Nachikatsuura, is a sacred site within the Kumano Nachi Taisha shrine, surrounded by stunning nature and hiking trails.
data.address: Nachisan, Nachikatsuura, Higashimuro District, Wakayama 649-5301, Japan

data.name: Jigokudani Monkey Park
data.description: Jigokudani Monkey Park is famous for its wild Japanese macaques, or snow monkeys, who visit natural hot springs in WINTER. Established in 1964, it o ff ers stunning snowy views and accessible paths for close wildlife encounters year-round. What about the less-visited parts of Japan ? Fukuoka Prefecture, or even the more remote islands such as Hokkaido or Okinawa The best option is obviously to take a domestic fl ight, pack only the essentials and make use of the multi-day baggage claim service once again
data.address: 6845 Hirao, Yamanochi, Shimotakai District, Nagano 381-0401, Japan

data.name: Hokkaido
data.description: Hokkaido, Japan's northernmost island, boasts stunning landscapes, from majestic volcanoes to serene onsens. Sapporo's famous Snow Festival and delectable ramen make it a must-visit for all.

data.name: Noboribetsu Jigokudani Valley
data.description: Noboribetsu Jigokudani Valley, or Hell Valley, showcases a breathtaking volcanic landscape with steaming vents and vibrant sulfur streams. Visitors can explore scenic trails, marvel at unique geological formations, and enjoy nearby therapeutic hot springs, making it a haven for nature enthusiasts.

data.name: Okinawa Prefecture
data.description: Okinawa Prefecture, Japan's southernmost islands, boasts a tropical climate, stunning beaches, rich history, vibrant culture, and delicious cuisine, o ff ering diverse outdoor adventures for all visitors.

data.name: Sunayama beach
data.description: Sunayama Beach, on Miyakojima in Okinawa, Japan, boasts stunning white sands and clear turquoise waters, perfect for swimming, sunbathing, and enjoying picturesque sunsets amidst scenic rock formations.
data.address: Sunayama beach, Nikadori Hirara, Miyakojima, Okinawa 906-0000, Japan

data.name: Cape Manzamo
data.description: Cape Manzamo is a stunning promontory in Onna, Okinawa, known for its elephant trunk-shaped rock formation and breathtaking views of the East China Sea, perfect for photography and relaxation amid lush greenery.

data.name: Yanbaru National Park
data.description: Yanbaru National Park, established in 2016, is situated in northern Okinawa, Japan. This stunning park features lush subtropical forests, limestone cli ff s, and expansive mangroves. Home to unique species like the Okinawa rail, it o ff ers hiking, canoeing, and bird watching, allowing visitors to immerse themselves in its remarkable biodiversity and breathtaking landscapes.
data.address: Hentona, Kunigami, Kunigami District, Okinawa 905-1411, Japan

data.name: Gyokusendo Cave
data.description: Gyokusendo Cave, a magni fi cent limestone cavern in Nanjo, Okinawa, extends over 5 kilometers. Visitors can explore 890 meters of stunning formations, while learning about its geological history and unique ecosystem.
